newsitem.title: UK: Northern loses CE takeover battle.
newsitem.headline: Northern loses CE takeover battle.

text.p: Northern Electric Plc lost its independence Tuesday after a hostile takeover battle with U.S. utility CE Electric.

CE Electric, which is controlled by Omaha, Neb.-based CalEnergy Co. Inc., said that by 8 a.m. EST Tuesday shareholders had agreed to tender 50.3 percent of Northern's ordinary shares, giving it victory in the takeover battle.
CE had bid 782 million pounds ($1.31 billion), or 650 pence per share, for Northern.
Uncertainty over the outcome of the bid went right down to the wire, with insurer Prudential Corp. stepping in at the 11th hour in an attempt to defend Northern.
CE Electric Chairman David Sokol said, "We are delighted by the outcome of the final offers for Northern Electric's shareholders."
Northern is the 10th of 12 privatised regional electricity companies to succumb to a takeover. Only Yorkshire Electricity Plc and Southern Electric Plc remain independent.
CE Electric's shares were unchanged at $29.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
